comment: Every place a source is weaker than it looks, and every place this package deliberately claims nothing. Each entry says what the document says, what the alternative says, which one this package follows, and what would settle it. The facts themselves live in hardware.json; this file is about their standing.

sources.document: Nintendo, Super Nintendo Entertainment System Development Manual, Book I, its archived text and its scanned pages. Pinned in documents.json and hardware.json.
sources.corpus: conformance/corpus.json, header combinations read out of a library of real cartridges. It answers what cartridges do, never what the console does.
sources.implementations: The access counts every emulator uses. Third rung, and named here only where nothing better exists.

divergences.documentSays: Section 21.1 at page 2-21-1: three clock speeds are available, 3.58MHz, 2.68MHz and 1.79 MHz. Figure 2-21-1 at page 2-21-2 labels 4000 to 41FF in banks 00 to 3F and 80 to BF as 1.79 M, CONTROLLER.
divergences.referenceDoes: Every implementation uses twelve master cycles for the controller-port region, which is 1.79 MHz.
divergences.reasoning: Closed on 2026-10-19. The record had read only the Map Mode table at page 1-2-17, which lists the two speeds a cartridge selects, and concluded the manual printed no third. Chapter 21 prints it in prose and in Figure 2-21-1, with the addresses it applies to. Twelve master cycles is 1.7898 MHz, which the manual prints as 1.79 MHz, so the count now follows from a printed figure the way the other two do, and it is marked verified in hardware.json.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: Settled by section 21.1 and Figure 2-21-1 of Book I. A measurement on a console counting master cycles on an access to 4016 would reopen it only by disagreeing.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing. Book I prints the two bus speeds in megahertz and never gives the master clock they divide.
divergences.referenceDoes: n/a. 21477273 Hz is six times the NTSC colour carrier, which is a property of the television standard rather than of this console.
divergences.reasoning: The arithmetic that turns the manual's two printed speeds into six and eight master cycles needs a master clock, and the one used comes from the NTSC relationship rather than from the document. It is worth naming because the derivation reads as though everything in it came from Nintendo, and one step did not.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A passage in either book giving the master clock frequency, or the crystal value from a schematic or a board photograph.

divergences.documentSays: Two bus speeds, and nothing about how many accesses an instruction makes.
divergences.reasoning: This package reports what one access to a resolved address costs. What an instruction costs is a different question, belonging to the processor rather than to the map, and it is answered in mos65xx-python. Refresh, DMA stalls and every other cycle the console spends on something other than the access are outside this too. Saying so matters because a per-access figure looks like a timing model and is not one.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: n/a. This is a scope boundary rather than an unknown.

divergences.documentSays: What a header field means and which values Nintendo defined.
divergences.referenceDoes: What real cartridges actually carry, including combinations the manual does not define.
divergences.reasoning: The manual is an instruction issued to licensees, so a genuine cartridge can disagree with it and still be genuine. Neither source overrides the other because they are not answering the same question: one says what was specified, the other says what was built.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: n/a. Both are kept, and a reader is told which is which.
